line: Lets the browser choose. Use it to undo an override.
description: cursor: auto lets the browser pick the cursor from context: an I-beam over text and a plain arrow everywhere else. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Hover the sentence, the link, then the empty space around them.
use: The initial value. Set it to undo an inherited override.
useFor: Resetting a cursor that a parent element overrode
Pages where text should show the I-beam and everything else an arrow
avoid: Clickable elements, which need pointer

mistakes.text: Forgetting that cursor is inherited, so a parent’s pointer shows on every child. Set auto on children that shouldn’t look clickable.

systems: Resolves to the system’s own arrow or I-beam, drawn by the OS.

line: The plain arrow, for app chrome like toolbars and menus.
description: cursor: default shows the platform’s plain arrow, whatever is underneath. Use it for app chrome like toolbars and menus. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Hover the words in each toolbar and compare.
use: App chrome like toolbars and menus, where the labels aren’t meant to be selected.
useFor: Toolbars, menus and tab bars in web apps
Labels that shouldn’t look selectable
avoid: Paragraphs people may want to select and copy

mistakes.text: Forcing default on all text, which hides the I-beam that shows text can be selected

systems: The standard arrow on every desktop system. Its exact shape follows the OS and, on Linux, the cursor theme.

line: Hides the cursor. Always draw your own replacement.
description: cursor: none hides the cursor completely. Use it for games, video playback and custom cursors, and draw a replacement. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Move your pointer inside the dark area.
use: Custom cursors, games, and video players that hide the pointer during playback. Always draw a replacement.
useFor: Custom cursors drawn with HTML or canvas
Video players while playback is idle
Full-screen games and kiosks
avoid: Hiding the pointer without drawing a replacement

mistakes.text: Hiding the cursor with no replacement and no way to bring it back

systems: Hidden on every desktop system. It comes back when the pointer leaves the element, so if you hide it on idle, bring it back yourself on movement.

line: More actions are available on right-click.
description: cursor: context-menu signals that more actions wait behind a right-click, on rows, files and objects on a canvas. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Right-click or click a file to open its menu.
use: Rows and objects that keep extra actions behind a right-click.
useFor: File and message rows with a custom right-click menu
Objects on a canvas that have extra actions
avoid: Elements that only have the browser’s default menu

mistakes.text: Keeping actions only in the right-click menu, where touch and keyboard users can’t reach them

line: Help is available, usually as a tooltip.
description: cursor: help shows that more information is available, usually in a tooltip on an info icon or an unfamiliar term. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Hover the question mark next to the label.
use: Info icons and terms that explain themselves in a tooltip.
useFor: Info icons that open a tooltip
Abbreviations and terms with a definition on hover
avoid: Links to a separate help page, which need pointer

mistakes.text: Showing the help on hover only, with no way to open it by keyboard or touch

systems: Usually an arrow with a question mark. The exact look varies by system, and touch screens show nothing.

line: For links, buttons, and anything clickable.
description: cursor: pointer shows the hand for links, buttons and anything clickable. Not for plain text or disabled controls. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Hover the shoe or the button, pick a size, then add it to your bag.
use: Links, buttons, and clickable cards. Not for plain text or disabled controls.
useFor: Links and buttons
Clickable cards and list rows
Custom controls built with role="button"
avoid: Disabled controls, which need not-allowed
Plain text and whole pages

mistakes.text: Leaving pointer on a disabled button
Adding pointer to a clickable <div> without a role or keyboard support

systems: The pointing hand on every desktop system. cursor: hand was an old Internet Explorer name that current browsers ignore.

line: Busy in the background, but still usable.
description: cursor: progress shows the app is busy in the background but still accepts input, as during syncs and uploads. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Start the sync, then keep moving around the card.
use: Syncs, uploads, and exports that don’t block the interface.
useFor: Background syncs and autosave
Uploads and exports that don’t block the page
avoid: Operations that block input, which need wait

mistakes.text: Relying on the cursor alone to show busy state, with no spinner or message in the interface

line: Busy and blocking input. Pair it with a spinner.
description: cursor: wait shows the app is busy and can’t take input yet. Use it for short blocking tasks, next to a spinner. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Click Publish and hover while it works.
use: Short, blocking operations. Pair it with a visible spinner or message.
useFor: Short operations that block input
A dialog that is saving and can’t be closed yet
avoid: Background work people can keep working through, which needs progress

mistakes.text: Leaving wait on after the work finishes or fails
Showing wait with no spinner or message, which touch users never see

line: Selects a cell or a range in a grid.
description: cursor: cell shows that a cell or a range of cells can be selected, as in spreadsheets and editable data grids. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag across the grid to select a range.
use: Spreadsheets and editable data grids.
useFor: Spreadsheet cells
Editable data grids with range selection
avoid: Read-only tables, where default or text fits better

mistakes.text: Using cell on header rows or controls inside the grid, which aren’t selectable cells

line: Precise selection for cropping, screenshots, and charts.
description: cursor: crosshair gives precise two-dimensional selection for cropping, screenshots and plotting points on charts. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag anywhere to capture a region.
use: Screenshot tools, image cropping, and plotting points on a chart.
useFor: Screenshot and region selection tools
Image cropping
Plotting points on a chart
avoid: General clickable areas, where the thin lines are hard to read

mistakes.text: Typing crosshar or cross-hair, which browsers ignore

systems: Usually thin crossing lines. On busy or dark backgrounds they can be hard to see, so test it where it will be used.

line: Text can be selected or edited. Set it on the whole box.
description: cursor: text shows the I-beam for text that can be selected or edited. Set it on the whole box, padding included. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Hover the padding inside each box and compare.
use: Editable areas that aren’t native inputs. Set it on the whole box so the padding shows an I-beam too.
useFor: Custom editors and contenteditable areas
Editable regions that aren’t native inputs
avoid: Buttons and links, even when they contain text

mistakes.text: Setting it on the text only, so the box’s padding still shows an arrow

systems: The I-beam on every desktop system. Its size and contrast follow the OS and, on Linux, the cursor theme.

line: Selectable text in a vertical writing mode.
description: cursor: vertical-text is the sideways I-beam for text in a vertical writing mode, as in Japanese or Chinese layouts. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Hover and select the poem.
use: Content set with writing-mode: vertical-rl, common in Japanese, Chinese and Korean typography.
useFor: Text set with writing-mode: vertical-rl
Vertical headings in Japanese, Chinese or Korean layouts
avoid: Horizontal text, which needs text

mistakes.text: Setting vertical-text on horizontal text, so the I-beam is turned the wrong way.

line: Creates a shortcut instead of moving the item.
description: cursor: alias shows that a shortcut or link will be created instead of moving the item, as when pinning or bookmarking. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Click a file to pin a shortcut.
use: Pinning, bookmarking, and linking to an item that stays where it is.
useFor: Pinning an item to a sidebar or favorites
Dragging to create a link or shortcut
avoid: Drags that move the item, which need grabbing or move

mistakes.text: Showing alias for a drag that actually moves or copies the item

line: Something will be copied, by click or by drag.
description: cursor: copy shows that something will be copied, by click or by drag, as in copy fields and duplicating drags. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Click the code to copy it.
use: Copy-to-clipboard fields and drags that duplicate instead of move.
useFor: Copy-to-clipboard fields
Drags that duplicate an item instead of moving it
avoid: Drags that move the original, which need grabbing

mistakes.text: Showing copy, then moving the item when it’s dropped

line: Moves an object freely on a canvas.
description: cursor: move shows that an object can be moved freely, as on a design canvas, a whiteboard or a layout editor. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the logo around the canvas.
use: Objects on design canvases, whiteboards, and layout editors.
useFor: Objects on design canvases and whiteboards
Dialogs and panels with a draggable title bar
avoid: Sortable lists and carousels, where grab and grabbing are clearer

mistakes.text: Using move for panning a whole view, where all-scroll or grab fits better

systems: A four-way arrow on most systems. Where the OS has no native version, the browser draws its own, so it can differ between browsers.

line: The dragged item can’t be dropped here.
description: cursor: no-drop shows that the dragged item can’t be dropped here, like a read-only folder or the wrong file type. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the file onto each folder.
use: Drop zones that refuse the item, like read-only folders or the wrong file type.
useFor: Read-only folders during a drag
Drop zones that refuse the file type
avoid: Disabled controls that aren’t drop targets, which need not-allowed

mistakes.text: Relying on the cursor alone to say why the drop is refused

line: The action is unavailable. Always explain why nearby.
description: cursor: not-allowed shows that the action won’t happen. Use it on disabled controls, and explain why right nearby. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Hover the button, then accept the terms.
use: Disabled controls. Always say why nearby, since a cursor alone can’t explain.
useFor: Disabled buttons and form controls
Actions blocked until a condition is met
avoid: Controls that look disabled but still work

mistakes.text: Leaving pointer on a disabled control instead
Not explaining nearby why the action is unavailable

line: Can be grabbed and dragged, before the button is pressed.
description: cursor: grab shows the open hand for things that can be dragged, before the button is pressed. Pair it with grabbing. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the photo strip sideways.
use: Pannable strips, carousels, and draggable cards, before the button is pressed.
useFor: Carousels and photo strips
Map and canvas panning
Sortable cards before they’re picked up
avoid: Items that can only be clicked, not dragged

mistakes.text: No grabbing state while the item is held
Keeping the old -webkit-grab prefix, which current browsers don’t need

line: Being held. Show it while a drag is in progress.
description: cursor: grabbing shows the closed hand while an item is held. Swap it in on pointerdown and back to grab on release. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag a task up or down to reorder it.
use: The pressed state during a drag. Swap it in on pointerdown, back to grab on release.
useFor: The pressed state of carousels and sortable lists
Panning a map while the button is down
avoid: The resting state, which needs grab

mistakes.text: Relying only on :active, which shows grabbing only while the pointer stays over the element. For drags, set it on the document until release.
Keeping the old -webkit-grabbing prefix

line: The edge moves up only, like a bottom sheet.
description: cursor: n-resize shows an edge that can only move up, like the top of a bottom sheet. Prefer ns-resize for two ways. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the handle on the edge.
use: An edge that can only grow upward, like a bottom sheet.
useFor: The top edge of a bottom sheet
Panels docked to the bottom that only grow upward
avoid: Edges that move both up and down, which need ns-resize

mistakes.text: Using it on an edge that can also move down, which needs ns-resize

line: The edge moves down only, like an expanding field.
description: cursor: s-resize shows an edge that can only move down, like an expanding notes field. Prefer ns-resize for two ways. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the handle on the edge.
use: An edge that can only grow downward, like an expanding notes field.
useFor: The bottom edge of an expanding text field
Dropdown panels that only grow downward
avoid: Edges that move both up and down, which need ns-resize

mistakes.text: Using it on a field that can also shrink upward, which needs ns-resize

line: The edge moves right only, like a left sidebar.
description: cursor: e-resize shows an edge that can only move right, like a sidebar docked left. Prefer ew-resize for two ways. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the handle on the edge.
use: The right edge of a sidebar docked to the left.
useFor: The right edge of a sidebar docked to the left
Columns that only grow to the right
avoid: Edges that move both left and right, which need ew-resize

mistakes.text: Using it on a sidebar edge that can also shrink, which needs ew-resize

line: The edge moves left only, like a right-hand inspector.
description: cursor: w-resize shows an edge that can only move left, like an inspector docked right. Prefer ew-resize for two ways. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the handle on the edge.
use: The left edge of an inspector docked to the right.
useFor: The left edge of an inspector docked to the right
Panels anchored to the right side
avoid: Edges that move both left and right, which need ew-resize

mistakes.text: Using it on an inspector edge that can also shrink, which needs ew-resize

line: The corner moves up and right, for panels docked bottom-left.
description: cursor: ne-resize shows a corner that can only move up and right, like a panel docked bottom-left. Or use nesw-resize. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the corner handle.
use: The free corner of a panel docked bottom-left.
useFor: The free corner of a panel docked bottom-left
Floating widgets anchored to the bottom-left corner
avoid: Corners that move both ways, which need nesw-resize

mistakes.text: Using it on a corner that can also move down and left, which needs nesw-resize

line: The corner moves up and left, for chat widgets docked bottom-right.
description: cursor: nw-resize shows a corner that can only move up and left, like a chat docked bottom-right. Or use nwse-resize. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the corner handle.
use: The free corner of a chat widget docked bottom-right.
useFor: The free corner of a chat widget docked bottom-right
Floating panels anchored to the bottom-right corner
avoid: Corners that move both ways, which need nwse-resize

mistakes.text: Using it on a corner that can also move down and right, which needs nwse-resize

line: The corner moves down and right, for notes pinned top-left.
description: cursor: se-resize shows a corner that can only move down and right, like a note pinned top-left. Or use nwse-resize. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the corner handle.
use: The free corner of a note pinned top-left.
useFor: The free corner of a note pinned top-left
Text areas that only grow down and to the right
avoid: Corners that move both ways, which need nwse-resize

mistakes.text: Using it on a corner that can also move up and left, which needs nwse-resize

line: The corner moves down and left, for menus anchored top-right.
description: cursor: sw-resize shows a corner that can only move down and left, like a menu anchored top-right. Or use nesw-resize. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the corner handle.
use: The free corner of a menu anchored top-right.
useFor: The free corner of a menu anchored top-right
Popovers that open from the top-right corner
avoid: Corners that move both ways, which need nesw-resize

mistakes.text: Using it on a corner that can also move up and right, which needs nesw-resize

line: Resizes left and right, for sliders and vertical dividers.
description: cursor: ew-resize shows something that resizes left and right, like a before-and-after slider or a vertical divider. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the divider left or right.
use: Before-and-after sliders, vertical dividers, and range handles.
useFor: Before-and-after image sliders
Vertical dividers between panes
Range handles
avoid: Table column dividers, where col-resize is clearer

mistakes.text: Making the handle only as wide as the visible line. Keep the draggable area at least 24 px wide.

line: Resizes up and down, for bottom panels and consoles.
description: cursor: ns-resize shows something that resizes up and down, like a bottom panel, a terminal or a debug console. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the terminal’s top edge.
use: Bottom panels like a terminal, console, or timeline.
useFor: Bottom panels like a terminal or console
Timelines docked under an editor
avoid: Dividers between stacked panes, where row-resize is clearer

mistakes.text: Making the draggable edge only a pixel or two tall, so it’s hard to grab

line: Diagonal resize for the top-right and bottom-left corners.
description: cursor: nesw-resize resizes diagonally from the top-right and bottom-left corners, as on crop boxes and selections. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag either corner handle.
use: The matching corner pair of crop boxes and selections.
useFor: The top-right and bottom-left handles of crop boxes
Selection frames on a canvas
avoid: The other corner pair, which needs nwse-resize

mistakes.text: Using the same diagonal cursor on all four corners

line: Diagonal resize for the top-left and bottom-right corners.
description: cursor: nwse-resize resizes diagonally from the top-left and bottom-right corners, as on images and app windows. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag either corner handle.
use: The matching corner pair for resizing images and windows.
useFor: The top-left and bottom-right handles of images
Window and panel corners
avoid: The other corner pair, which needs nesw-resize

mistakes.text: Using the same diagonal cursor on all four corners

line: For column dividers in tables and grids.
description: cursor: col-resize shows a column divider that can be dragged sideways, as in tables, spreadsheets and data grids. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag a column divider in the header.
use: Column dividers in tables and data grids.
useFor: Column dividers in tables and data grids
Resizable column headers
avoid: Before-and-after sliders, where ew-resize reads better

mistakes.text: Making the grab area as thin as the visible divider line

line: For dividers between stacked panes.
description: cursor: row-resize shows a divider between stacked panes that can be dragged up and down, like a query and its results. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the bar between the two panes.
use: Split panes stacked on top of each other, like a query and its results.
useFor: Split panes stacked vertically
A query editor above its results
avoid: Panels docked to the window’s bottom edge, where ns-resize fits

mistakes.text: Making the grab area as thin as the visible divider line

line: Pans in any direction, like a map.
description: cursor: all-scroll shows content that can be panned in any direction, like a map, a floor plan or a large canvas. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Drag the map in any direction.
use: Maps, large canvases, and middle-click autoscroll.
useFor: Maps
Large canvases and diagrams
Floor plans and seating charts
avoid: Single objects that can be dragged, which need move

mistakes.text: Showing all-scroll where the content only scrolls up and down

systems: Often drawn as a four-way arrow, and on some systems it looks the same as move. Where the OS has no native version, the browser draws its own.

line: Magnifies an image or product photo on click.
description: cursor: zoom-in shows that clicking magnifies an image or product photo. Swap it for zoom-out once the image is zoomed. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Click the photo to zoom in.
use: Product photos and image viewers in their normal state.
useFor: Product photos
Image galleries and lightboxes
avoid: Images that open a new page, which need pointer

mistakes.text: Keeping zoom-in after the image is already zoomed
Keeping the old -webkit-zoom-in prefix

line: The zoomed state. Click to return to normal size.
description: cursor: zoom-out shows the zoomed state, where a click returns the image to normal size. Swap back to zoom-in after. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Click the photo to zoom out.
use: The zoomed state of the same viewer. Swap the two on each click.
useFor: Zoomed product photos
Lightboxes in their magnified state
avoid: Images that aren’t zoomed yet, which need zoom-in

mistakes.text: Not swapping back to zoom-in after zooming out
Keeping the old -webkit-zoom-out prefix

line: Your own image. Keep it 32 × 32 px with a keyword fallback.
description: cursor: url() sets your own image as the cursor, with an x y hotspot and a keyword fallback. Keep it 32 × 32 px or smaller. Live demo and copy-ready CSS.
hint: Draw on the canvas with the brush.
use: Tool cursors like brushes and pens. Keep images at 32 × 32 px or smaller, and always end with a keyword.
useFor: Drawing tools like brushes and pens
Branded cursors in games and kiosks
avoid: Replacing standard cursors people rely on, like pointer and text

mistakes.text: Leaving out the keyword fallback, which makes the whole declaration invalid
Forgetting the hotspot, so clicks land on the image’s top-left corner
